Already without starting left tackle Trevor Goosby for the remainder of the season, the injury issues have piled up for Texas headed into Saturday's road matchup with the Missouri Tigers. Now, the Longhorns are receiving worst-case scenario news when it comes to starting running back Hollywood Smothers, who exited last week's game against Mississippi State with an apparent lower-body injury. Smothers will miss the remainder of the 2026 season due to a torn MCL in his knee, according to multiple reports. He started the year off as the team's starter after transferring in from NC State. In the second half against Mississippi State, Smothers took a hard hit to his lower body and sat on the turf holding his left knee. He was then helped off the field by trainers and was unable to put any weight on his left leg. Smothers finishes his 2026 season with 69 carries for 283 yards and two touchdowns along with 10 catches for 79 yards and another score. His pair of rushing touchdowns came in one of the biggest moments of Texas' season, as he had two scores in the fourth quarter against Ohio State, highlighted by the game-winning touchdown in the final minute to complete the comeback. The Longhorns have already gotten accustomed to life without Smothers this season. He previously dealt with ankle and shoulder injuries, forcing him to miss games against Tennessee and Ole Miss. Texas running back Raleek Brown now becomes the no-doubt starter moving forward for the Longhorns. So far this season, he's tallied 92 carries for 452 yards and five touchdowns along with 12 catches for 54 yard and another score. This was highlighted by an impressive performance in the win over Ole Miss when he had 23 carries for 157 yards. Behind him, Michael Terry III and Derrek Cooper will continue to receive an uptick in snaps. Terry has impressed and appears to have overtaken Cooper on the depth chart. It feels likely Terry will be Brown's backup moving forward. But at this point, they want a spot in the Big Ten Championship, and they're good enough to beat anyone left on the slate. Minnesota has proven it's almost good enough to beat anyone, losing a brutal 23-16 heartbreaker to Indiana last week. It beat Iowa and Michigan, but a weird 41-13 loss at Purdue is an issue for an at-large CFP spot. However, win out, and there's a shot at getting into the Big Ten title game. There's no real mystery to what UCLA does. It blasts away, with the ground game, gets just enough from the passing game to get by, and then it relies on the defense to take care of everything else. It starts with third down stops. Only Nebraska – at least before the loss to Illinois – is better at defensively on third downs than the Bruins. That allows UCLA to dominate the time of possession battle, the rested defense forces a ton of takeaways, the offense capitalizes … repeat. However … Why Minnesota Will Win UCLA runs well, Minnesota doesn't. Minnesota can throw well, UCLA doesn't. Other than that, these two do almost all of the same things. You want third down defense? Minnesota is sixth in the nation, allowing teams to convert just 28% of their chances. Time of possession? The Gophers aren't as good as UCLA, but they're fine, usually keeping the ball for close to 32 minutes per game. And then there are the takeaways – Minnesota is good at that, too. The temperature should hover around 40 degrees and feel more like 32ish for the entire game in Huntington Bank. UCLA will be pushed and tested, and Minnesota will take advantage of that early, but the score will be kept low throughout, and the Bruins will still be alive in the second half, when the ground game starts to take over. It'll be another tremendously entertaining Minnesota game to kick off a whale of a Saturday. home.headline: Gophers freshman tight end Roman Voss is ready for a bigger role as injuries pile up
home.blurb: The Gophers’ No. 1 tight end, Pierce Walsh, has missed the last two games due to injury. Their No. 2 tight end, Julian Johnson, has joined Walsh on the injury report this week, and both players are “doubtful” against UCLA as of Thursday night. Signing Roman Voss in the 2026 high school cycle was one of P.J. Fleck’s biggest recruiting wins of his Gophers tenure. We’re quickly learning why Alabama and numerous top programs were after Voss, as Minnesota’s true freshman tight end continues to find his footing this season. Now 6-foot-4 and 235 pounds, Voss was a decorated prep athlete at Jackson County Central (JCC) High School in southern Minnesota. The Huskies played at the Class 2A level, but Voss was so dominant he won Minnesota Gatorade Player of the Year and Minnesota Mr. Football as a senior. He played quarterback and finished his senior season with 1,902 yards and 21 touchdowns through the air and 1,893 yards and 30 more touchdowns on the ground. Voss’s final college choice came down to Alabama and Minnesota. He also had notable offers from programs like Miami (FL), USC, Oklahoma, Auburn and more. He was dubbed a four-star prospect and the second-best player in Minnesota, according to the 247Sports Composite. Transitioning from quarterback at the high school level to tight end in the Big Ten isn’t easy, so there were plenty of questions about how quickly Voss could contribute for the Gophers. Through seven weeks, he has seven receptions for 117 yards and two touchdowns, all of which are the most by a tight end on Minnesota’s roster. Voss has still played only 94 offensive snaps this season, but when he’s on the field, the Gophers want to get him the ball. He has run a route on 95.5 percent of those snaps, which emphasizes that Minnesota sees him as more of an offensive weapon than a blocker at this moment. That leaves Voss, Oklahoma transfer Kaden Helms, third-year player Jacob Simpson and fellow true freshman George Rohl as the Gophers’ only healthy tight ends who have played significant snaps this season. Minnesota’s offense has averaged just 14.5 points per game since the bye week. Voss has averaged 36.5 yards in the same span, which is just one yard per game fewer than Darius Taylor, who received 18 more touches. Javon Tracy’s 53.5 yards per game is the only mark significantly higher than Voss’s, but he has also gotten significantly more opportunities. Voss has more yards than TJ Thomas, Noah Jennings and Jalen Smith over the last two games. If Johnson and Walsh end up missing this week’s game against UCLA, Minnesota’s game plan should include getting Voss more involved. It’s time to take off the training wheels. Nothing appears to be working consistently right now, and getting the football into the hands of your best playmakers is typically a sound strategy to fix that. My Alabama vs. LSU prediction and college football picks back Lane Kiffin and the Tigers to end their Saban Bowl losing streak as Alabama looks for its fourth straight win on the first Saturday in November. The Crimson Tide visit Tiger Stadium in Baton Rouge, La., where LSU is a 5.5-point favorite in Death Valley. Kickoff is set for 3:30 p.m. ET on ABC on Saturday, Nov. 7. TOP PICK Who will win Alabama vs LSU: LSU -5.5 The last time LSU won the Saban Bowl, Nick Saban was Alabama's head coach and Lane Kiffin was still beloved at Ole Miss . That will change Saturday when Kiffin's surging Tigers take advantage of a Crimson Tide team that's looked like a far cry from its No. 5 College Football Playoff ranking. With LSU's defensive ferocity and Alabama's offensive struggles, I like the Tigers to cover up to -6.5 at home against the Tide. Not only has LSU's defense been wrecking opponents, but the Tigers' offense has been on fire too, with Sam Leavitt fourth nationally in QBR (85.3) and 12th in adjusted completion percentage (79.5%). Leavitt's improved play and the emergence of Jackson Harris (480 receiving yards and seven TDs in his last four SEC games) are a problem for an Alabama defense that's ranked 78th in pass success rate (44.3%). Alabama vs LSU Over/Under pick: Under 52.5 This game isn't one of the must-watch games in my college football Top 25 predictions this week because I'm expecting offensive fireworks; it's because of the talent on these defenses. LSU's defense is especially loaded, and with Alabama's struggles against quality defenses, I would play the Under at 51.5 or better. The Tigers are second nationally in sacks (34) , and Keelon Russell hasn't managed pressure well. He's been sacked the ninth-most in the country (22) and has a 20.4% pressure-to-sack rate. But I don't expect an offensive onslaught from LSU either. This is the best defense the Tigers have faced this season, with Alabama ranking 20th nationally in available yards percentage (37.7%) and 14th in net adjusted EPA per play. Alabama vs LSU combo Alabama has gotten off to slow starts and failed to cover in three straight games as a result. In the Crimson Tide's last three games, it trailed Georgia 10-0, trailed Tennessee 9-0, and trailed Texas A&M 14-10. If Alabama gets off to another slow start and trails LSU, the Tigers' defense will pin their ears back and go to work. LSU ranks eighth nationally in pass success rate on defense (36%) and has one of the most lethal pass rush duos in the country, Princewill Umanmielen and Jordan Ross (58 combined pressures and 13.5 sacks). Death Valley is one of the hardest places to play, and with Alabama's broken offense, I don't expect the Tide to score much early against this opportunistic LSU defense. A team which Alabama has won the last three games against dating back to 2023, this latest showdown against LSU is likely to be their toughest in recent years. The Tigers are considered one of the SEC's top teams at 6-2 (3-2 SEC), and have a roster loaded with talent led by head coach Lane Kiffin. In addition to that, this latest matchup between the Crimson Tide and Tigers has significant College Football Playoff (CFP) implications. Released this past Tuesday night, Alabama was ranked No. 5 in the first CFP rankings as the top ranked two-loss team, while LSU sat at No. 14. A challenging matchup, let's make three predictions for the Crimson Tide during Saturday's massive road game at LSU. Alabama's offensive line struggles against LSU pass rush Oct 3, 2026; Starkville, Mississippi, USA; Alabama Crimson Tide offensive lineman Michael Carroll (64) waits for the snap during the third quarter against the Mississippi State Bulldogs at Davis Wade Stadium at Scott Field. Mandatory Credit: Petre Thomas-Imagn Images When taking a look back at the Tennessee game, Alabama's offensive line struggled at times in pass protection with a Volunteers defense that led the nation in sacks, and the Tide are likely set to face a similar challenge this Saturday in a LSU unit which ranks No. 2 nationally in the stat. As a result, combined with the tough road atmosphere in Tiger Stadium, I'll predict the Alabama offensive line to struggle at times in pass protection against an elite LSU pass rush, especially if the Crimson Tide are without two starters up front. Alabama's defense forces multiple turnovers Oct 10, 2026; Tuscaloosa, Alabama, USA; Alabama Crimson Tide defensive back Bray Hubbard (18) celebrates his interception during the second quarter against the Georgia Bulldogs at Saban Field at Bryant-Denny Stadium. Mandatory Credit: David Leong-Imagn Images LSU quarterback Sam Leavitt enters Week 10 leading the SEC with eight interceptions thrown this season, and is set to face an Alabama defense that has 12 picks this year which is tied atop the conference. I'll say that Alabama picks off Leavitt at-least once this Saturday afternoon, with the Tide defense also forcing a fumble at some point. Keelon Russell, Tide passing game has solid showing While I do predict Alabama's offense to struggle in pass protection at times similar to the Tennessee game, I do not think the passing game will struggle as much as it did in Knoxville where the Tide threw for only 147 yards. Yes, the Tide are facing a LSU defense that ranks No. 3 in the SEC in fewest yards allowed per game, but Alabama might be getting Ryan Coleman-Williams back Saturday, and with an extra week of rest and preparation, I would imagine we see a different performance from Keelon Russell and company. picks.headline: ‘If they don't get time, it's going to be a real uphill climb' – ESPN's Greg McElroy predicts the final score of Alabama vs LSU
picks.blurb: ‘If they don't get time, it's going to be a real uphill climb' – ESPN's Greg McElroy predicts the final score of Alabama vs LSU - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Luka's explosive night UConn tops Michigan Porziņģis stepping away Purdue stunned by Valparaiso Myles Garrett set to return Stephen Lew-Imagn Images Zach Ragan · AtoZ Sports Tue, November 3, 2026 at 8:43 PM UTC · 1 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The LSU Tigers will host the Alabama Crimson Tide in a huge SEC showdown in Baton Rouge this weekend. LSU will host Alabama this upcoming Saturday in what's a de facto College Football Playoff elimination game. Alabama and LSU both have two losses. It's possible that the loser of this game could still get into the playoff with three losses — it depends on how the rest of the season plays out — but the winner will be the only one that controls its own destiny moving forward. ESPN's Greg McElroy, a former Alabama quarterback, made his score prediction for the game, and he has LSU leaving Tiger Stadium with a 27-20 win. McElroy thinks LSU's defensive line will be able to win the battle up front. "I'm taking LSU to win the game 27-20," said McElroy. "I do think the under is in play, but it's really going to come down to Alabama's offensive line. If Keelon Russell gets time, they can win this game in Baton Rouge. But if they don't get time, it's going to be a real uphill climb for the Crimson Tide." McElroy noted that most of the sacks Alabama has given up this season have come from Russell holding the ball too long. Alabama and LSU will kick off at 2:30 PM CT/3:30 PM ET on Saturday. The game will air on ABC. This article was originally published on A to Z Sports. picks.headline: Alabama against LSU Final Score Predictions: Experts make their picks ahead of potential College Football Playoff eliminator
picks.blurb: Alabama against LSU Final Score Predictions: Experts make their picks ahead of potential College Football Playoff eliminator - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Luka's explosive night UConn tops Michigan Porziņģis stepping away Purdue stunned by Valparaiso Myles Garrett set to return David Leong-Imagn Images – John Reed-Imagn Images Brandon Little, Craig Smith, Justin Churchill, Rob Gregson, Ryan Roberts, Tyler Forness · AtoZ Sports Thu, November 5, 2026 at 4:54 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads See who the experts have getting the job done on Saturday afternoon in Baton Rouge. On one of the most stacked slates in recent college football history, the afternoon matchup between the LSU Tigers and Alabama Crimson Tide will be center stage for the nation to see. Two teams with two losses, despite the initial College Football Playoff rankings ; this one could go a long way in determining who makes the final 12. Alabama is aiming for the return of multiple starters after a much-needed bye week, but the Tigers seemingly found both health and a groove on defense before their own bye week. So who wins? Myself and 5 colleagues at A to Z Sports picked the winner for this marquee matchup. Alabama vs. LSU all-time facts 90 total meetings Alabama leads 58-27-5 Alabama leads 30-10-3 in Baton Rouge Alabama has won 3 straight Alabama 30, LSU 27 Assuming Alabama returns the likes of Terrance Green, Racin Delgatty, Zabien Brown, Ryan Coleman-Williams, and EJ Crowell, the Crimson Tide will be the healthiest it has been since Week 1. Green and Delgatty are massive upgrades in the middle of the trenches, and Alabama has missed the explosive dynamic that RCW and Crowell bring to the offense. But this game will come down to Alabama's defense. If Kane Wommack can get the boys buzzing and creating turnovers, we have seen that it only takes one for Sam Leavitt to start giving the ball away. That's where the return of Zabien Brown at corner is so impactful. I expect Alabama to force a couple of key turnovers, winning the Crimson Tide the ball game. – Rob Gregson, A to Z Sports Alabama LSU 31, Alabama 27 This game is tough to predict, and I could honestly see it going either way. But in this one, the more talented team with the veteran QB will get the win. LSU's offense is going to be able to stifle anything Bama brings to the table defensively. As for Bama, their offense has struggled lately. Give me LSU. – Justin Churchill, A to Z Sports Oklahoma LSU 27, Alabama 17 Lane Kiffin and the LSU Tigers welcome Alabama to Tiger Stadium on Saturday in the first of three straight top 13 games for the Bayou Bengals. Alabama, fresh off a No. 5 ranking in the initial college football playoff, has relatively light resistance remaining after this contest, with Vanderbilt and Chattanooga following before the Iron Bowl in Tuscaloosa. Thus, the chances for the Tide to impress after this one are minimal. So this is an enormous game for both teams for playoff consideration. The Tigers have suddenly found themselves on the defensive side of the ball, shutting out Mississippi State (albeit a Kamario Taylor Bulldogs team) and dominating Auburn 38-17 on the road. Sam Leavitt has thrown for 677 yards with seven touchdowns and no picks over that span, and he has LSU's offense playing at a high level. With Alabama being a bit up and down in recent weeks (Tennessee dud and shaky first half against Texas A&M), I'll go with LSU at home to get it done. – Craig Smith, A to Z Sports, Miami Hurricanes Alabama 31, LSU 27 This game being at 3:30 ET feels really weird, but that's what happens with the slate as stacked as it is. ESPN was smart to have this game not against Miami vs. Notre Dame. I'm leaning the Crimson Tide because I don't trust Lane Kiffin in big games. Heck, I don't trust Lane Kiffin much at all. Keelon Russell will come alive and the potential return of Ryan Coleman-Williams will spark a huge win for the Crimson Tide. – Tyler Forness, A to Z Sports Florida Gators Alabama 24, LSU 21 We might as well look at this 6-2 battle as a College Football Playoff game because whoever loses likely won't be taking part in the postseason. I think this game simply comes down to whoever has the better day at quarterback between Keelon Russell and Sam Leavitt. Russell making a tough start in Louisiana is going to be a tall task, and LSU's defense is the better unit in this game. Lane Kiffin has a lot of pressure on his team to deliver in this game and continue its path to the CFP in his first season with a highly expensive roster. In the end, I think Alabama weathers the storm throughout the game and hangs on late. – Brandon Little, A to Z Sports Ohio State Alabama 31, LSU 21 I'm taking Alabama to come away with a 31-21 victory over LSU in a game that should be competitive for much of the afternoon. I expect Keelon Russell to deliver one of his better performances, showing the arm talent and confidence that make him such an exciting quarterback. Alabama should be able to create some opportunities through the air, particularly when Russell gets time to work through his progressions and attack LSU's secondary. The Crimson Tide will have some early struggles dealing with LSU's athleticism, but I think Russell settles in and helps Alabama build some momentum offensively. Sam Leavitt and LSU should come out firing, and I wouldn't be surprised if the Tigers have the upper hand early in this one. However, I think the game ultimately swings in Alabama's favor because of a couple of costly second-half turnovers. Leavitt will make some impressive plays, but a pair of back-breaking mistakes will give the Crimson Tide short fields and opportunities to put the game away. Alabama's defense takes advantage, and Russell does enough offensively to keep LSU from making a late push. Alabama wins 31-21. – Ryan Roberts, A to Z Sports Notre Dame This article was originally published on A to Z Sports. (Photo by Stew Milne/Getty Images) | Getty Images Joshua Chatham · SB Nation Fri, November 6, 2026 at 3:18 PM UTC · 8 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Happy Friday, everyone. The women's basketball team feasted on yet another cupcake last night to move to 3-0, this time taking down Alabama A&M by a 96-43 margin . The men play tonight against Arkansas State, and we will have coverage of that one later on. Alabama football plays at LSU tomorrow, as you well know. Your previews: Alabama gets an immediate chance to justify its CFP ranking, while LSU can strengthen its argument with a win that leaves the Tide staring at three losses. I picked LSU to win this game in August, and I'm sticking with the Tigers' passing game at home against an Alabama secondary still sorting through injuries. Sam Leavitt throws for 278 yards and two touchdowns, and Jackson Harris catches both of them while finishing with 110 receiving yards. LSU wins 26-20, keeping its SEC title hopes alive and giving Alabama fans another reason to avoid the internet. Alabama football needs this win. Kalen DeBoer wins after idle weeks. And the Crimson Tide knows how to win against LSU on the road. All of these remain true. But this is a new Tigers team in a new era with Lane Kiffin at the helm. It's a unit starting to find itself after single-score losses to Ole Miss and Kentucky. LSU has the second best scoring offense and defense in the SEC. It has the No. 1 total offense and defense in the SEC. This is a Tigers team that is waiting for an opportunity to see what it can do against the upper echelon of SEC play in November, and the Crimson Tide is the first team in LSU's way. Alabama has looked like the best team in the country before on the road, beating Mississippi State to a pulp in Starkville, but the same couldn't be said about Kentucky in Lexington, or, especially, Tennessee in Knoxville. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect Transfer Portal 2027 Top Recruits 2027 Top Classes College Football Rankings No. 12 Ohio State hosts No. 23 Oregon in a pivotal game in the Big Ten and CFP race Getty Images Week 10 of the college football calendar has been highlighted since the schedule was released, with No. 23 Oregon's trip to face No. 12 Ohio State among the headliners. However, when the Buckeyes host the Ducks at 3:30 p.m. ET on CBS, it will not be two teams vying for a bye in the College Football Playoff, but instead two programs trying to keep their season from unraveling. The Ducks, at 5-3, have already seen their playoff dreams snuffed out, but a win last week against Northwestern brought their offense to life after a coordinator change. Dylan Raiola had his best game as a starter for Oregon in a win over Northwestern, and now the Ducks have real belief they can go into the Horseshoe and pick up a win that could salvage what's been a disappointing season. Ohio State, meanwhile, comes in with a backup quarterback of their own and is searching for answers after a 30-18 loss on the road to USC last week. Luke Fahey will get his second start and first at home, hoping to find more success and keep Ohio State in the playoff hunt after the first CFP rankings put them at No. 12 -- which would be the first team out of the 12-team playoff. The winner on Saturday will enter the stretch run of the season feeling like they've stabilized after a shock to the system in the form of losing their star quarterbacks for the year. The loser, on the other hand, will realize their goals are no longer within reach and face some hard questions entering the offseason. Ohio State vs. Oregon: Need to know Can Ohio State solve red-zone woes?: The Buckeyes moved the ball fine against USC's defense. It was the best rushing performance from Ohio State this season in Big Ten play in terms of yards per carry (4.74), and while Fahey missed some explosives, he still threw for 260 yards. The problem for Ohio State was finishing drives with six points instead of three. Ohio State made four trips into the red zone against USC and came away with just 13 points. Against Indiana , it also scored 13 points in three trips to the red zone, and the inability to come away with touchdowns nearly cost them there too. If the Buckeyes are going to control this game and keep Oregon from building belief it can win on the road, Fahey has to be sharper in the red zone and the Ohio State rushing attack has to be able to help out. Ducks find life after coordinator change: Oregon's offense had its best performance since the win at USC last Saturday afternoon against Northwestern, one week after firing offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer. Interim coordinator Jay Johnson seemed able to get Raiola into a rhythm and keep him there, something the Ducks have struggled with all season (even with Dante Moore ). The frustration after the Illinois game seemed to be an unwillingness to stick with what worked -- in that game, it was the rushing attack -- and against Northwestern, once they found some concepts that worked, they went back to the well until proven otherwise. That seems simple, but it's not always easy as a play-caller to not let your mind wander and get too cute trying to stay ahead of the defense. Johnson seems more comfortable just rolling with what works and being aggressive in any spot, which seems to have a trickle-down effect on Raiola and the offense, also playing with more comfort and aggression. That's going to be necessary against an Ohio State defense that is quite good but, as USC proved, can be hit for big plays. Oregon can't be afraid to take swings as a road dog, and last week's performance gives it some confidence it can do that effectively with Raiola. Which defense can steal possessions?: With a young quarterback and a red-zone offense that's struggling, the Buckeyes might need their defense to give them a spark. For as good as the Buckeyes have been defensively this season, they haven't been great at turning teams over. They have just four interceptions on the year (94th nationally) and are 48th in total turnovers forced at 11. Raiola has been prone to turnovers for his entire career dating back to Nebraska and will likely present a couple of opportunities -- either with interceptable balls or strip sacks -- for the Buckeyes to steal a possession or two. Ohio State has to capitalize on those chances if they want to help their sputtering offense. On the other side, the best way to make Ohio State tight in this one would be to pick off the young quarterback and make Ryan Day a bit anxious about letting the young man sling it. Oregon has nine interceptions this season (13th in the country), and if they can bait the freshman into an early mistake, it could alter the Buckeyes' game plan and give the Ducks an even better opportunity on the road. Ohio State should be able to run the ball well, and at home I would expect Fahey and the offense to operate a bit better in the red zone to put touchdowns on the board when they do move the ball. A Ducks offense trying to push it in the passing game should result in big plays (possibly for both teams), and this is a rare big game where I'm anticipating plenty of points. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect Transfer Portal 2027 Top Recruits 2027 Top Classes College Football Rankings Two SEC contenders clash with heavy College Football Playoff implications Getty Images On a weekend full of marquee games, No. 13 Tennessee and No. 6 Kentucky will get their share of the spotlight on Saturday night in Neyland Stadium. In the long history of this rivalry, there's a good case that this is the biggest game ever. In his first year on the job, Will Stein has led Kentucky to a 7-1 start and a great shot at reaching the College Football Playoff with just four games remaining. His major transfer portal additions -- particularly quarterback Kenny Minchey and the offensive line -- clicked almost immediately. To this point, the Wildcats have passed all but one test they've faced, but the level of difficulty rises this weekend. Kentucky must continue to play clean football if it wants to come away with a win in Knoxville. Tennessee had two weeks to wallow in the "what if" after its three-point loss to South Carolina , but the team has to get back in the saddle this weekend. The Volunteers have the chance to pick up their second top-10 win of the season, which would really boost their CFP rankings. There's no doubt that the Vols have a playoff-caliber defense and running game, but can Josh Heupel fix the passing attack? Tennessee must improve there to reach its ceiling. Here is everything you need to know about this top-15 rivalry matchup in Knoxville. Tennessee vs. Kentucky: Need to know Rare ranked matchup: These teams have met well over 100 times, but this is just the fourth ranked matchup in history. Most recently, Tennessee and Kentucky played a top-25 matchup in 2022, with the Volunteers winning in a blowout. Prior to that, the only times the Vols and Wildcats were ranked simultaneously were in 1950 and 1951. That means there's a very good case for this matchup to be the biggest in the history of this rivalry. Games with stakes in this series usually go the way of Tennessee, but can Stein turn the tables on Saturday night? Kentucky not in the giving spirit: The holidays are approaching quickly, but Kentucky has not been feeling very generous. One of the driving factors behind the Wildcats' success is their incredible plus-13 turnover margin. That ranks first in the SEC and fourth in the entire country. For the first time since 2013, Kentucky has avoided turning the ball over in three consecutive games. If any team can end that streak, it's probably Tennessee, which has a great defense and has forced 14 turnovers in eight games. The Vols just have to protect the ball on offense. Heavy dose of DeSean Bishop : Kentucky defensive coordinator Jay Bateman probably doesn't need my advice, but I would suggest he lock in on Tennessee running back DeSean Bishop. He's been the engine of the Vols offense, and his 957 rushing yards rank sixth in the country. His 12 rushing touchdowns are tied for ninth. Over the last four games, Bishop has averaged 29 carries and 159 yards. If the Wildcats can contain Bishop and force Tennessee to throw the ball, that could be a recipe for success, but only one team has effectively shut Bishop down to this point. Kentucky's offense has been incredibly efficient, and it will pose a real challenge to the Tennessee defense. That said, the first night game in Neyland Stadium will give the Vols an edge on that side of the ball. Offensively, Tennessee leans on Bishop and gets enough out of its passing game to pull away from Kentucky late and cover the one-score spread. picks.blurb: Kentucky at Tennessee: Final thoughts and prediction - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Luka's explosive night UConn tops Michigan Porziņģis stepping away Purdue stunned by Valparaiso Myles Garrett set to return Story by Wildcats Wire Kentucky at Tennessee: Final thoughts and prediction Braxton Howard, UK Wildcats Wire · Wildcats Wire Fri, November 6, 2026 at 6:30 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Kentucky football travels to a hostile Neyland Stadium to take on the Tennessee Volunteers at 6:15 P.M. ET on Saturday night. This is a massive game with a lot at stake for both teams, the Wildcats are undefeated on the road this season and they will try to continue that streak in this game. We laid out the path to victory for Kentucky and the key areas they need to win to improve to 8-1 on the season. It is time to give some final thoughts on the matchup and give a game prediction. As I stated earlier in the week on my Tennessee defense preview , but I truly think this game comes down to Will Stein's offense versus Jim Knowles' defense. They have met three times and Coach Stein has gotten the best of Knowles in two of those three meetings. Kentucky has to continue to play efficient on offense and play clean. I think they have a great opportunity to methodically move the football down the field as they have all season against this defense. This game starts and ends in the trenches, on both sides of the football. Tennessee's defensive line is the strength of their team, but Kentucky's offensive line is playing better than any offensive line in the country. They have to stabilize defensive tackle Xavier Gilliam, who has been wrecking offensive gameplans all season long. A key matchup to watch is Kentucky center Coleton Price against Gilliam, Price has been one of the best centers in the country and he will have his hands full in this game. Kentucky has to win this game on the line of scrimmage, and I have confidence in the Wildcats offensive line to gain the edge in that matchup. Tennessee's offensive line has been above average as run blockers, but they do struggle in pass protection. Kentucky forcing Tennessee into a dropback heavy game script could be critical, but they have to stop the run in order to do that. Kentucky's defensive line has gotten consistent pressure all season, and I am very intrigued to see how this defensive line gets after a pocket passer like George MacIntyre because they have faced a mobile quarterback in every game this season. Kentucky has to win the line of scrimmage, and this is the best offensive line the Vols have faced this season. I think the Wildcats defensive line has been underrated this year, and they can make a statement on Saturday. The run defense has improved tremendously in the month of October, and slowing down the Vols heavy rushing attack is crucial. If they can force Tennessee into a heavy dropback game, Kentucky will be able to create turnovers like they have all season. Truthfully, I believe the biggest advantage is Kentucky's coaching staff getting two weeks to prepare for this football game. Tennessee is coming off the bye week as well, but Josh Heupel and Jim Knowles are going to do what they do. Kentucky's coaching staff has added plenty of wrinkles week-to-week, so I can only imagine what they will have in store with two weeks to prepare. This is an advantage for Kentucky, particularly on the offensive side of the football. We all know this history of this series, it has not been kind to Kentucky. However, this is a different era of college football and Kentucky football. If you remove the history and helmet logos, I think Kentucky has the advantage at quarterback and offensive line as well as a hotshot head coach that has done an unthinkable turnaround in year one for this program. It will be a close game in the fourth quarter, and how could you not trust Will Stein and Kenny Minchey under those circumstances. Prediction: Kentucky 24, Tennessee 20 This article originally appeared on UK Wildcats Wire: Kentucky at Tennessee: Final thoughts and prediction

"We have a, you know, awesome opportunity this week to play an elite SEC opponent in Tennessee on the road. You know, I think they're playing extremely well as a team. They could easily be eight and zero. They're number one in sacks, number two in TFLs … They have eight seniors on defense, so it's a veteran group. I think that is a big piece in how they're able to operate cleanly," Stein said. Here's what those designations mean: Per SEC policy, schools must accurately designate players' participation status. On Saturday, Marcus Freeman could do the same against the same program. No. 11 Notre Dame and No. 1 Miami meet in South Bend with playoff implications on the line in what is the highest-ranked matchup between the programs (according to the AP poll) since that classic Catholics vs. Convicts showdown in 1988. The Irish won the national championship that season, its most recent title. The College Football Playoff selection committee sees a different matchup. Miami sits atop the first CFP rankings, but slotted Notre Dame at No. 11, seven spots lower than the AP voters. Notre Dame is the last team in the CFP field, and a loss against Miami could knock the Irish out of playoff contention entirely. "They don't have that signature win right now," CFP committee chair Hunter Yurachek said Tuesday night on ESPN. "They've got a great opportunity in front of them at home versus Miami to get that signature win that I think they need to move up in the rankings." Don't forget, we've been here before. Miami defeated Notre Dame 27-24 in last season's season opener. The Irish remained above Miami in five CFP rankings, but the committee flipped the two in the final week, placing Miami over Notre Dame in the CFP. Miami vs. Notre Dame: Need to know Darian Mensah vs. a defense without its leader : Darian Mensah leads the FBS in completion percentage (80.7%) and pass efficiency (202.7) and is tied for the national lead with 25 touchdown passes against one interception. Notre Dame takes him on without linebacker Drayk Bowen , its leading tackler (45) and the green-dot helmet that relays defensive calls. He was ruled out with an ankle injury suffered against Navy . Malachi Toney's absence : Miami will be without superstar receiver Malachi Toney, who suffered an ankle injury in practice Wednesday and will undergo surgery in hopes of returning for the CFP. This game certainly takes on a different context. The sophomore ranks in the top three nationally in receptions (73), receiving yards per game (128.4) and receiving touchdowns (13), the last of which ties Miami's single-season school record. Cooper Barkate is the second-best receiver on the roster, but he averages 46.5 yards per game, compared to Toney's 128.4. CJ Carr's problem : Carr has been magnificent most of his career, but the splits are wild. He's thrown 18 touchdowns and one interception this season, and he is 15-0 as a starter against unranked teams. Against AP-ranked opponents, he is 2-3, completing 60.9% of his passes at 6.6 yards per attempt with six touchdowns and five interceptions. With few opportunities to impress the CFP committee, he needs to step up against the top-ranked Hurricanes. Unranked Boston College , SMU and Syracuse are the only teams remaining on the schedule. Notre Dame's invincibility : Notre Dame is 10-1 at home against Miami, and the home team has won the last eight on-campus meetings. Miami's only win at Notre Dame Stadium came in 1984. On the other side, the Hurricanes are 18-3 on the road as the AP No. 1, with all three losses at ranked teams, including the 1988 game against the Irish. Miami hasn't defeated an AP top-5 team on the road since 2005. Penalties and the red zone : Notre Dame is the most disciplined team in the FBS, averaging only 28.9 penalty yards per game. Miami ranks 82nd (58.8). The Irish defense, however, ranks 108th in red-zone defense, allowing points on 88.9% of possessions, and Miami scores on 92.9% of its own. Where to watch Miami vs. Notre Dame live Date : Saturday, Nov. 7 | Time : 7:30 p.m. ET Location : Notre Dame Stadium -- South Bend, Indiana TV: NBC | Live stream: Fubo (try free) Miami vs. Notre Dame prediction, picks Notre Dame opened as a 4.5-point favorite and is now laying 5.5, with the total at 57.5. History sides with the Irish. Now that Malachi Toney is out, siding with the Irish becomes an easy play. Notre Dame will play the nation's most efficient quarterback either way, but how different does he look without his top option? Meanwhile, Notre Dame's red-zone defense has struggled against far lesser offenses, so will Toney's absence actually matter? Miami is 5-3 against the spread this season. Notre Dame is 4-4. The Irish can win this game, but covering by five points will still be difficult. Skip to main content SI.COM FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS FOOTBALL RECRUITING SI.COM IRISH FB BASKETBALL NEWS MEN'S SCHEDULE MEN'S RANKINGS SI.COM IRISH BB For the first time in exactly seven years, Notre Dame welcomes the No. 1 team in the nation to South Bend. Like last time, when top-ranked an unbeaten Clemson came to town late in the 2020 season, another ACC foe brings an unbeaten an No. 1 ranking. This time its the mighty Miami Hurricanes and the rivalry between the two programs is as strong as ever. Game week 🆚 Miami 📍 South Bend, Indiana 📆 Saturday, Nov. 7 ⏰ 7:30 PM ET 📺 NBC | Peacock #GoIrish ☘️ | @tirerack pic.twitter.com/xO17lohHXw So does Notre Dame knock off No. 1? Or does Miami leave South Bend with the No. 1 overall seed in the College Football Playoff seemingly on ice? Here's what the matchups favor on Saturday night in South Bend: When Miami Has the Ball Malachi Toney or not , this Miami offense is like few in all of college football. Sure, its biggest playmaker is out, but can Notre Dame slow down the thunder and lightning running attack of Javian Mallory and Mark Fletcher? Furthermore, Darian Mensah has 25 touchdown passes to just one interception all season long. Can Notre Dame's defense, which will be playing a bit shorthanded itself, keep Miami in check enough? Notre Dame has one of the better offensive lines in college football but has its work cut out against this Miami defensive front. The Hurricanes are allowing just 2.4 yards per rush attempt this year, which means Notre Dame likely won't be able to play the same ball possession type game it likes to. That means CJ Carr's moment is now: Miami has a pass defense that has surrendered huge numbers in narrow escapes against both Florida State and North Carolina. Can Carr do enough to win what could very possibly turn into a track meet between the powerhouse programs? Advantage: Notre Dame Special Teams For the Win? Factor in a veteran kicker in Spencer Porath who is Notre Dame's best at the position in years and special teams coordinator Marty Biagi, who has had a bit of a quiet year by his standards, to date, and I expect to see the Irish steal a possession and deciding score as a result. picks.blurb: Rece Davis Predicts Notre Dame Playoff Problem Ahead of Top-5 Miami Showdown Skip to main content SI.COM TRANSFER PORTAL More from CFB-HQ On SI NEWS Notre Dame could find itself in the same College Football Playoff predicament that ended its 2025 season if it can’t beat No. 1 Miami on Saturday, according to ESPN College GameDay host Rece Davis. Davis made the case on ESPN’s College GameDay Podcast with co-hosts Pete Thamel and Dan Wetzel, saying the No. 4 Fighting Irish (7-1) would be in “ very much the same situation as a year ago ” with a loss. Rece Davis on Notre Dame’s resume Notre Dame Fighting Irish head coach Marcus Freeman reacts during the first half against the Brigham Young Cougars | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Davis noted that ESPN’s Football Power Index, a forward-looking measure, ranks Notre Dame No. 1. Miami, however, ranks No. 1 in strength of record, which grades what a team has done against its schedule. Davis noted that ESPN’s Football Power Index, a forward-looking measure, ranks Notre Dame No. 1. Miami, however, ranks No. 1 in strength of record, which grades what a team has done against its schedule. Davis said that split will shape the debate over the Irish. He expects them to stay in the field unless the Hurricanes blow them out, but he doesn’t see the questions about their resume going away. “I think Notre Dame will still be OK absent getting run out of the stadium, which I cannot conceive of happening,” Davis said. “So it’s going to be a little bit different than last year, but the argument, the discussion, is going to be the same if they don’t win this game.” He added: “When you get down to who did you play and who did you beat, especially the who did you beat portion of who did you play, they won’t have much on the paper.” Why does Notre Dame’s schedule matter? General view as Brigham Young Cougars fans celebrate on the field after the game against the Notre Dame Fighting Irish | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Notre Dame has faced one team ranked at the time of kickoff this season, and it lost 28-24 at BYU on Oct. 17. None of its seven wins came against a team in this week’s AP Top 25. Notre Dame has faced one team ranked at the time of kickoff this season, and it lost 28-24 at BYU on Oct. 17. None of its seven wins came against a team in this week’s AP Top 25. The Irish beat Wisconsin, Rice, Michigan State, Purdue, North Carolina, Stanford and Navy. After Miami, they close with Boston College, SMU and Syracuse, who are a combined 14-10 and unranked. Notre Dame does carry a protection it lacked last year. The College Football Playoff guarantees the Irish a spot if they finish in the top 12 of the final rankings. A loss to Miami would test that cushion, though, because Notre Dame would sit at 7-2 with no win over a ranked opponent and no ranked teams left on its schedule. Miami vs. Notre Dame stakes Miami Hurricanes head coach Mario Cristobal celebrates after defeating the Florida State Seminoles | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Last season, Miami and Notre Dame both finished 10-2, and the selection committee used the Hurricanes’ 27-24 win in Week 1 to award them the final at-large spot. The Irish were the first team out and declined a bowl invitation. The Irish were the first team out and declined a bowl invitation. Notre Dame athletic director Pete Bevacqua said at the time, “ We feel like the playoff was stolen from our student-athletes.” Davis called the rematch “another little delicious subplot” and said Notre Dame’s frustration “wasn’t necessarily just directed at Miami.” Notre Dame head coach Marcus Freeman made “ leave no doubt ” the program’s mantra for 2026 after the snub. Saturday gives the Irish that chance against an 8-0 Miami team that leads FBS at 47.6 points per game, while Notre Dame’s defense leads FBS at 236.1 yards allowed per game. The committee releases its first College Football Playoff rankings of the season Tuesday at 7 p.m. ET on ESPN, and Miami vs. Notre Dame kicks off Saturday at 7:30 p.m. ET on NBC and Peacock. Two of college football's most prominent programs meet for a second straight season when Notre Dame hosts Miami on Saturday at 7:30 p.m. ET on NBC at Notre Dame Stadium in Notre Dame, Ind. Early Miami vs Notre Dame spread pick: Miami +5.5 From 1971 to 1990, the Miami Hurricanes and Notre Dame Fighting Irish played almost every season, with the Irish dominating the 70s and the Hurricanes dominating the 80s. After just four matchups from 1991 to 2024, these two juggernauts are playing for a second straight season after Miami beat Notre Dame 27-24 last year. While I'm not sure an outright win is in the cards for Mario Cristobal's team this year, I do like Miami to cover for a second straight season at +3.5 or better . The biggest reason is the weapons around Darian Mensah . Mensah and CJ Carr are arguably the two best QBs in the country this season, but Mensah has so much more around him. away.blurb: Days before the Miami Hurricanes ' biggest game of the regular season, their best player came down with an injury that reports say will not only keep him from facing archrival Notre Dame , but potentially out until the College Football Playoff ... or later. The explosive wideout has battled injuries throughout the season, briefly leaving games against Wake Forest on Sept. 18, Clemson on Oct. 3 and Florida State on Oct. 17. He never went back to the locker room, though his limited play late against Wake can be explicitly tied to the offense's stagnation and one of their closest games of the season. (This story has been updated to add new information.) Multiple reports said Malachi Toney, a front-runner for the Heisman Trophy, rolled his ankle at practice Wednesday, Nov. 4. While initially reported as not a long-term issue, ESPN reported in the evening that Toney suffered a high ankle sprain would require surgery. USA TODAY Sports' John Brice confirmed Toney will miss an "extended period of time." Recovery from a high ankle sprain typically takes four weeks, which would encompass the Hurricanes ' remaining regular-season schedule. The first round of the CFP, for which 8-0 Miami currently holds the No. 1 ranking, is Dec. 18-19, six weeks away. If Miami retains one of the top four spots in the final CFP rankings, they would first play in the quarterfinals Dec. 30 or Jan. 1, in about eight weeks. ESPN's Pete Thamel was the first to report the injury. According to a report by On3's Pete Nakos , Toney got caught up with a cornerback at practice, leading to the injury. "Malachi Toney sustained an injury during Wednesday's practice and is currently undergoing further evaluation by the team's medical staff," Miami said in a statement, shared by the Miami Herald's Barry Jackson on social media. "We will share additional updates as appropriate." Toney is the engine that drives No. 1 Miami's top-ranked scoring offense . Through eight games, the 19-year-old has already tied the program record with 13 receiving touchdowns this season, a number that puts him one behind Oregon State's Jesse Legree for the most in the nation. away.headline: Miami gets concerning Malachi Toney injury update ahead of Notre Dame clash
away.blurb: Miami will undoubtedly want Toney available for this crucial matchup, but playing through an ankle injury could bring risks for one of the Hurricanes’ most valuable offensive weapons. The undefeated Miami Hurricanes face a major test this weekend when they battle the Notre Dame Fighting Irish in a showdown between College Football Playoff contenders. Miami enters the matchup ranked No. 1 in both the AP Top 25 poll and the initial CFP rankings. Much of that has been thanks to the on-field brilliance of quarterback Darian Mensah and star wide receiver Malachi Toney. However, a concerning injury update regarding Toney surfaced on Wednesday, potentially putting his availability for the Notre Dame matchup in jeopardy. According to ESPN’s Pete Thamel , sources told him and Max Olson that the Hurricanes’ Toney is dealing with an ankle injury, leaving his status for Saturday’s matchup “uncertain.” “Toney is expected to press and attempt to play, given the magnitude of the game,” Thamel also said in his X report. More news: CFP Committee Chair Under Fire for Alabama’s Controversial Ranking Toney ranks second in NCAA football with 73 receptions, third with 1,027 receiving yards, and third with 13 touchdowns. The 5-foot-11 sophomore has delivered several impressive performances this past season, including 154 yards and two touchdowns in Miami’s double-overtime win over Florida State. As of this writing, Toney is also considered one of the leading Heisman Trophy contenders. Mensah has emerged as the favorite to win, and Toney’s production has played a significant role in the quarterback’s success this season. Saturday’s game carries major CFP implications for Miami and Notre Dame. Both teams appeared in the initial CFP rankings, with Miami holding the top spot and Notre Dame landing at No. 11. However, several games remain on their schedules before the playoff field is finalized. A loss could seriously damage Notre Dame’s chances of getting into the College Football Playoff. Meanwhile, Miami is undefeated, and a loss could hurt its standing in the CFP rankings. Keeping that perfect record could strengthen Miami’s chances of a first-round bye in the CFP. The Miami Hurricanes take on the Notre Dame Fighting Irish at 7:30 p.m. ET on Saturday, Nov. 7. away.headline: No. 11 Notre Dame prepares for No. 1 Miami as storied rivalry returns to South Bend
away.blurb: Notre Dame has injury concerns of its own . Captain and starting linebacker Drayk Bowen is out after injuring his ankle against Navy. Starting cornerback DJ McKinney also is out. Defensive linemen Francis Brewu and Jason Onye were listed as questionable with knee injuries on Notre Dame’s injury report earlier this week. The 1988 meeting between Notre Dame coach Lou Holtz and Miami coach Jimmy Johnson became known as “Catholics vs. Convicts.” Before kickoff, a scuffle broke out between the teams in the tunnel area. Skip to content Digital Marketing Giraffe Cam 16 Vault Contests We the People Donate to Cultivate Turkeys on the Table News Election Results Nationwide Results WNDU Streaming Entertainment Quality Control Programming Programming Schedule Closed Captioning/Audio Description SOUTH BEND, Ind. (WNDU) - No. 1 Miami is coming to South Bend on Saturday, where No. 11 Notre Dame will look to pull off an upset and add another chapter to a storied rivalry. The Hurricanes bring one of the nation’s top offenses to face a strong Irish defense, but both teams will be missing key players. Quarterback matchup and a key absence The game features two of college football’s top quarterbacks in Notre Dame’s CJ Carr and Miami’s Darian Mensah. Mensah has thrown for more than 2,400 yards and 25 touchdowns with just one interception, completing 80% of his passes. Miami will be without wide receiver Malachi Toney, who has more than 1,000 receiving yards and 13 touchdown catches this season. Toney sustained an ankle injury in practice this week and will miss Saturday’s game, according to The Associated Press . Speaking earlier in the week, before Toney’s status was clear, Notre Dame coach Marcus Freeman said the Irish needed to prepare for both possibilities. “You got to have a plan for a dynamic player like that,” Freeman said. He added that the Irish needed to be ready to adjust depending on who plays. Freeman noted that Miami has other talented players who can step in. Among them is receiver Cooper Barkate, who transferred to Miami from Duke, where he played with Mensah. Freeman said preparation will be central to the Irish’s chances against Miami. “Every player has to have self-awareness of what he needs to be able to do his job,” Freeman said. “And that’s more important than anything. I don’t want it to be loose. I don’t want it to be tight. I want you to be in a position, in a mental and physical state, that you can get your job done. “The team that’s most prepared will find a way to execute and win on Saturday,” he added. Notre Dame cornerback Leonard Moore said he is approaching the matchup like any other game. “No different than the other game, but just, you know, being in tune to my preparation and being in tune to having good practices and making sure I prepared mentally for the game,” Moore said. “But ultimately, I’m not worried about the crowd. We always going to have a big crowd, especially with a good team like this. Everybody’s going to be tuned. E

home.headline: Why Bill O’Brien Hopes Boston College Captain Michael Crounse Returns Against Notre Dame
home.blurb: CHESTNUT HILL, Mass. — The morning after Boston College football’s initial student-athlete availability report for Saturday’s contest against FSU came out, head coach Bill O’Brien spoke on the injury designation for Michael Crounse, the Eagles’ starting center and a prized team captain. The impact Crounse has for BC is paramount for a variety of reasons — that could be seen when he made his return from injury against Georgia Tech in Week 8 , as the Eagles ran for nearly 400 yards. But in BC’s Week 9 loss on the road to Duke , his lower leg got rolled on quite badly in the second half, which forced him out of the game and into a boot. “I mean, he’s progressing,” said O’Brien. “He was in a boot. He’s out of the boot already. So we’ll see for Notre Dame. [I] really, really want him to play against Notre Dame.” While Crounse is officially out this week, the Eagles’ road contest in South Bend, Ind., next week against the Fighting Irish will be a particularly special one for the redshirt junior. Boston College Football Tight End Kaelan Chudzinski Confirmed Available for Duke Game But the main reason that he makes such a big difference on the field stems from his veteran presence in the huddle, which is undeniably a key trait in all levels of sport, especially football. After suffering a knee injury in the Eagles’ Week 1 loss at Cincinnati, Crounse missed four straight games before returning against the Yellow Jackets, and he finished that game without any major setbacks. O’Brien technically confirmed it isn’t a season-ending injury, which is positive news for the Eagles. But it will at least sideline him for this week’s matchup, and possibly one that has been marked on Crounse’s calendar for months. That is because Crounse’s father, Mike, played for Notre Dame from 1986-90, highlighted by a consensus national championship in an undefeated 12-0 1988 season. “It’s a special game for him,” O’Brien said. “But there’s not much we can do about it. We feel terrible for Mike, but it is what it is.” Freshman DJ Williams, who has a 48.7 offensive grade on PFF (Pro Football Focus), which ranks near the very bottom of FBS centers that qualify for a grade, will be making his fifth-career start in Crounse’s place. It is not an ideal situation to be thrust into as an underclassmen, especially as a replacement for a captain of all people. But Williams now has enough experience under his belt to enter Saturday’s showdown with the Seminoles carrying a bit more confidence than he had at the beginning of the season, when he was essentially tossed straight into the ring of fire with no legitimate playing time to lean on as a guidance tool. “DJ’s got another opportunity,” O’Brien said. “And DJ’s had a good week. DJ’s a great dude, and he’s a really good guy who’s practiced very well.” Follow us on Twitter/X , Facebook , YouTube , Instagram , and Tiktok for the latest Boston College news. The Bulldogs came back from a nine-point fourth-quarter deficit in the first meeting, outscoring the Rebels 17-0 in the fourth to win 43-35, but Ole Miss would have its revenge. It was in the College Football Playoff quarterfinal at the Sugar Bowl that the Rebels ended Georgia's season with a 39-34 win thanks largely to the heroics of quarterback Trinidad Chambliss . So what will these two deliver this year? While plenty has changed from last year's teams to this year, both quarterbacks return, and there are high stakes involved here. Georgia debuted at No. 2 in the first College Football Playoff rankings of the season, and a win here would solidify their chances of reaching the SEC Championship. On the other side, the Rebels need a win to gain firmer ground. They're No. 10 in the rankings, putting them on the precipice of losing an at-large bid. Plus, a loss here would be their third in SEC play, essentially ending their conference title hopes, and putting them in a position where they need to win out and hope for some other teams to lose to return to the playoff. My Georgia vs. Ole Miss prediction and college football picks expect Kirby Smart's defense to rise to the occasion this time against Trinidad Chambliss as the Bulldogs seek revenge for last year's Sugar Bowl loss. Georgia is a 3.5-point road favorite as it visits Vaught-Hemingway Stadium in Oxford, Miss., on Saturday, Nov. 7. Kickoff is set for 7:30 p.m. ET on ABC. TOP PICK Who will win Georgia vs Ole Miss: Georgia -3.5 Georgia and Ole Miss played two wild shootouts last year, with the Bulldogs winning the regular-season matchup and the Rebels taking it in the Sugar Bowl. This time around, I like Georgia to cover as many as 6.5 points on the road against Ole Miss. Defense will be the difference in the matchup this year, with Georgia having one of the best in the country ( ranked No. 2 by SP+ ), and Ole Miss' being one of the worst in the SEC. With the Rebels down All-American running back Kewan Lacy , the Bulldogs' defense can lock in on stopping Trinidad Chambliss . Chambliss has faced one other defense ranked top five by SP+, Texas , and struggled in a loss. Against the Longhorns, he threw three interceptions and put up a season-low 60% adjusted completion percentage. Georgia vs Ole Miss Over/Under pick: Under 56.5 Though both games between these teams last year were full of points, Georgia's defense should keep it relatively low-scoring this time around, and I would play the Under at 55.5 or better . The Bulldogs' defense ranks top 20 nationally in available yards percentage (33.5%) , havoc rate (19.4%), and success rate allowed (35.2%). With no Lacy for Ole Miss, it'll put even more on Chambliss, who has frequently had to carry the team this season, and we saw that approach fall flat against Texas. However, Georgia's offense hasn't been lighting up the scoreboard lately either, averaging just 23.6 points per game in its last three outings. So while this is one of the must-watch matchups in my Week 10 Top 25 predictions , it's not because I'm expecting another shootout. Georgia vs Ole Miss combo Ole Miss is a feast-or-famine type of team. The Rebels beat LSU and Missouri , but were blown out by Florida and fell behind so quickly against Texas that they couldn't dig themselves out. That's what happens when you lean so heavily on a star QB to make up for an inconsistent run game and one of the worst defenses in the SEC. Against Georgia, Chambliss won't be Superman; Smart has too much NFL talent on a defense that's allowed more than 20 points just once this season. If Ole Miss falls behind, Georgia's offense will lean on Gunner Stockton to manage the game and take a ball-control approach against a Rebels defense ranked 88th in the country in EPA per rush. Expect a breakout passing performance, a game-changing takeaway and a decisive finish in one of Week 10's biggest matchups. The College Football Playoff rankings place Georgia second and Ole Miss 10th entering Saturday's showdown. The Bulldogs arrive at 7–1, while the Rebels are 6–2, with kickoff scheduled for 7:30 p.m. ET at Vaught-Hemingway Stadium. This forecast favors Georgia's offensive balance over the home crowd. Here are three bold predictions for a matchup that should test both quarterbacks' ability to handle pressure. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Stockton delivers a career night Dale Zanine-Imagn Images Gunner Stockton will throw for 325 yards and three touchdowns without an interception. That would establish a career high in passing yardage, surpassing the 304 yards listed in Georgia's game notes, and represent an emphatic response to his 101-yard performance against Florida. The prediction hinges on Georgia resisting the temptation to make this exclusively a rushing contest. Early play-action should give Stockton opportunities to attack intermediate windows before Ole Miss settles into its preferred defensive rhythm. The matchup offers a reasonable opening: the Rebels allow 235 passing yards per game, while Stockton has completed 71.8 percent of his attempts this season. Expect Georgia to spread the production rather than funnel everything toward one receiver. Its offensive personnel should allow the Bulldogs to challenge linebackers underneath before testing safeties with deeper routes. The key will be protection discipline. Georgia should prioritize clean pockets over elaborate, slow-developing concepts, letting Stockton build confidence through quick decisions. Once Ole Miss starts anticipating those shorter throws, the Bulldogs can take their shots. The bold part is not simply predicting efficiency. It is forecasting a career-best road performance when Georgia needs its quarterback to create separation rather than merely protect a lead. Georgia scores another defensive touchdown The Bulldogs will intercept Trinidad Chambliss twice and return one takeaway for a touchdown. That forecast respects the challenge rather than dismissing it. Chambliss enters with 2,189 passing yards, 18 touchdown passes and eight interceptions, making him dangerous but not immune to costly decisions. Ole Miss will also be without running back Kewan Lacy, who was listed out on the initial availability report because of his shoulder injury. That absence could encourage Georgia to devote more attention to containing Chambliss and disrupting his reads. The defensive plan should emphasize controlled pressure. Reckless pursuit would invite escape lanes; disciplined rush angles could force Chambliss to hold the ball or attempt throws into tightening coverage. Expect one interception to come after Georgia initially presents an aggressive front, then drops a defender into an underneath passing lane. The touchdown prediction is ambitious, but Georgia has already scored three defensive touchdowns this season. Another would change the entire complexion of a game in which both offenses should face stretches of frustration. Georgia ends Oxford's winning streak Georgia will win 38–24, ending Ole Miss' 16-game home winning streak. home.blurb: Friday Ole Miss vs. Georgia Injury Report: Keaton Thomas Probable - The Rebel Walk FRIDAY Ole Miss vs. Georgia Injury Report: Keaton Thomas Probable, Franklin Questionable Recent ‘I've got to go out there and earn it’: Hunter Elliott returns with something to prove as Ole Miss opens fall OXFORD, Miss. – Ole Miss linebacker Keaton Thomas is probable for Saturday night's game against No. 2 Georgia after being questionable on Thursday, according to the SEC's Friday availability report. Defensive end Kam Franklin remains questionable. The report was posted at 7:10 p.m. CT on Friday. Ole Miss' list of players who are out did not change, with running back Kewan Lacy and eight others ruled out again. Georgia, meanwhile, moved three players from questionable to out: inside linebacker AJ Kruah , safety Tyriq Green and defensive lineman Joseph Jonah-Ajonye . Keaton Thomas moves up to probable Thomas, a linebacker, was questionable on both Wednesday and Thursday and is now probable for Saturday night. Kruah, Green and Jonah-Ajonye were all questionable on Thursday and are now out, joining outside linebacker Amaris Williams, who has been out all week. Tight end Elyiss Williams remains questionable. Pete Fiutak · College Football News Sat, November 7, 2026 at 2:18 AM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads When we last saw Oklahoma and Florida play, the Sooners rolled 55-20 in the 2020 Cotton Bowl over a high-powered Gator team that lost to eventual national champion Alabama in an epic SEC Championship. The other meeting was the BCS Championship at the end of the 2009 season, when Tim Tebow and the Gator defense took down Heisman-winner Sam Bradford and the amazing Sooner attack 24-14 for the national title. The stakes aren't as high this time around, but for a Florida program that's on the rise, and No. 24 in the first College Football Playoff rankings, and for a 4-4 Oklahoma desperate to close strong, this will be intense. Oklahoma vs Florida: Quick Hits Oklahoma at 4-4, needs to win two of its last four to be bowl eligible. It hosts Ole Miss and Texas A&M after this before closing at Missouri. Florida is coming off the 27-8 loss to Georgia. It goes to Kentucky next, hosts Vanderbilt, and finishes at Florida State. Again, the first two meetings were in big bowl games. This is the first regular season matchup between the two. How To Watch Oklahoma vs Florida Date: Saturday, November 7, 2026 Game Time: 7:45 PM ET TV: SEC Network Location: Ben Hill Griffin Stadium, Gainesville, FL – Week 10 Schedule, Predictions – CFN Top 25 | Bowl Projections – Expert Picks: Week 10 Why Oklahoma Will Win The defense continues to fight the good fight. It had a problem in the 42-25 loss to South Carolina, but the defense is fantastic on third downs thanks to a pass rush that takes over games. But to beat Florida, you have to slow down the run. The Gators are 0-3 when running for fewer than 155 yards, and the Sooners give up just 107 yards per game. Only Mississippi State and, last week, South Carolina have been able to gash the Sooners for more. Why Florida Will Win Oklahoma's offense has a hard time running the ball. With a defense as good as the Sooners have, all the O has to do is keep it moving and not screw it up. But no running game means more pressing overall, and then come the mistakes. The Sooners only average 107 yards per game on the ground, and they just can't find any room to move. The Gators have to hold up, and then pounce on an Oklahoma attack that turned it over four times against both Georgia and Kentucky, three times against New Mexico, and twice against Michigan. Oklahoma vs Florida Prediction, Betting Lines It's stupid, but if you buy into these things, going back to the last two games of last season, Oklahoma is on a ten-game run of alternating wins and losses. The Sooners beat Texas, then lost to Kentucky, beat Mississippi State, lost to South Carolina, beat … Florida? The Sooners have the defense to hold up and make Florida struggle. The Gators got by Texas a few weeks ago, but it's been a struggle, losing three of the last four. Weird trends aside, this Oklahoma team really does have a way of rallying when it absolutely has to. picks.blurb: Staff Picks: Will Oklahoma Get Back on Track at No. 24 Florida? - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Luka's explosive night UConn tops Michigan Porziņģis stepping away Purdue stunned by Valparaiso Myles Garrett set to return Staff Picks: Will Oklahoma Get Back on Track at No. 24 Florida? Oklahoma Sooners tight ends coach Jason Witten will take over as interim offensive coordinator for the rest of the season. | Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Ryan Chapman · Oklahoma Sooners On SI Fri, November 6, 2026 at 12:00 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Gators have an impressive resume, having beaten No. 4 Ole Miss 52-28 at The Swamp, then going on the road to Austin and taking down No. 7 Texas 27-24 - one week after OU beat them in Dallas - on a night the underwhelming Florida defense overwhelmed Arch Manning and the Longhorns, sacking him five times, limiting UT to 2-of-10 on third down (they had 13 first downs total) and holding the Horns to 272 total yards. But they were also blown out in back-to-back losses to No. 25 Missouri and unranked South Carolina, which preceded last week's 27-8 loss to No. 3 Georgia. Oklahoma is a touchdown underdog to Florida, but the Sooners are the best defense the Gators face. Still, OU may be reeling after its worst defensive performance in years in the blowout loss to South Carolina - which included an incomprehensible 25 missed tackles (usually 10 is a bad number). OU's first trip to The Swamp will be punctuated by another big game from Gators RB Jaden Baugh, who's third in the SEC at 100.3 rushing yards per game and first with 13 rushing TDs. Final score: Florida 28, Oklahoma 21 Things could get gross Saturday night. Florida has officially made a quarterback change, and Tramell Jones Jr. could be without a pair of key weapons to pair with an already banged up offensive line. Oklahoma's offense has been so bad it got its coordinator fired, but Jason Witten has never called plays collegiately and John Mateer is still likely the quarterback the Sooners will roll with. OU's defense needs to bounce back after its tackling struggles last week, but even an improved showing could see Gator running back Jaden Baugh have enough success to push Jon Sumrall's team across the finish line. Final: Florida 16, Oklahoma 13 OU is set up for further disaster as it heads to the swamp. Jason Witten will serve as the Sooners' play caller for the first time at the college level, John Mateer is still the quarterback and Ben Hill Griffin Stadium is one of the nation's most hostile atmospheres. But amid the weirdness, I expect OU to win this game. Teams often come out more inspired after a notable firing, and I predict Witten will lead a creative game plan as he auditions for the full-time offensive coordinator role. Florida's offense is good - but it is also prone to turning the ball over. If the Sooners are able to put pressure on Tramell Jones Jr. early, it will create a long day for the Gators' offense. Final: Oklahoma 24, Florida 20 The Sooners figure to get a little boost from Jason Witten's playcalling, but don't expect massive changes in either scheme or production here. The offensive line still has its issues, John Mateer hasn't been consistent at all, and neither of the other quarterbacks have experience in games like this. But Oklahoma's defense does figure to have a bounce-back game after struggling to contain LaNorris Sellers and the South Carolina offense. The tackling will be better, and Florida's offense is in a bit of flux itself with Tramell Jones Jr. expected to make his second start of the season at quarterback and Florida's offensive line struggling in recent weeks. But the Gators still have plenty of talent, especially on the offensive side, and The Swamp is one of the toughest environments in college football. That's a tough position for a reeling team to be placed in. The game will be close into the second half but the Gators figure to pull away and hand Oklahoma its second consecutive defeat. Final: Florida 24, Oklahoma 14 Brady Trantham A new offensive coordinator doesn'tchange the fact that John Mateer is still QB1 at OU. Mateer gives Oklahoma their best shot in any game, but in 20 games as the Sooner signal caller, it is apparent that he simply isn't very good. A coaching change can, in theory, help him in spots, but if OU needs their QB to make a play in a tight game, chances are he will make that play - just for the other team. Florida sticks to the run and gets Oklahoma on a few explosives and rides it to an easy win. The Sooners need to win two of their final four to earn bowl eligibility . With a new voice leading the offense, the Sooners are hoping for a turnaround to end the 2026 season. Jason Witten takes over an offense that has underachieved this season, given the number of returning starters along the offensive line and the weapons at returning quarterback John Mateer. How much better can Oklahoma be in a week is the question on everyone's minds. It's unlikely the Sooners will suddenly erupt on offense, but if they find more consistency, they'll have a chance to finish the season on a high note. So how will the Sooners perform in "The Swamp?" Our staff here at Sooners Wire picked this week's showdown between the Sooners and the Gators. Too Many Questions Oklahoma tight ends coach Jason Witten, left, talks with coach Brent Venables during a Sooners football spring practice in Norman, Okla., Thursday, April 9, 2026. There are just too many moving parts for Oklahoma to reliably believe the Sooners could win a road game in the swamp. The Sooners have made a change at offensive coordinator and the availability of a bunch of notable players on both sides of the ball are still in question. There's also the question of how Oklahoma quarterback John Mateer will play without Ben Arbuckle on the sideline for the first time in years. Even though Florida has a few issues to worry about as well, they're certainly not as dire as Oklahoma's at the moment. Florida 21, Oklahoma 10 James D. Jackson, Contributor Improved Sooners Oklahoma tight ends coach Jason Witten during a college football game between the University of Oklahoma Sooners (OU) and the South Carolina Gamecocks at Gaylord Family-Oklahoma Memorial Stadium in Norman, Okla., Saturday, Oct. 31, 2026. South Carolina won 42-25. Touchdowns? Touchdowns. Oklahoma made a huge move this week by letting go of Ben Arbuckle and having Jason Witten call plays. Witten called plays as a high school head coach and had a ton of success doing it. I think the offense will play with a fire we haven't seen this year, and the defense will return to its dominant ways. Because of that, I've got OU winning and the offense scoring three touchdowns. OU 27, Florida 17 Oklahoma 27, Florida 17 Jaron Spor, Contributor Defense gives Oklahoma a chance Sep 4, 2026; Norman, Oklahoma, USA; UTEP Miners quarterback EJ Colson Jr. (1) throws as Oklahoma Sooners defensive lineman David Stone (0) chases during the game at Gaylord Family-Oklahoma Memorial Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images Last week's disaster set in motion a sequence of events that should end with Brent Venables' team having a new offensive coaching staff, a new starting QB, and new faces up and down the offensive depth chart. For now, though, the only change is the absence of OC Ben Arbuckle, so all of Oklahoma's other offensive problems remain. Expect OU's defense to bounce back against Florida, but expect the offense to continue faltering for the remainder of this season. Florida 16, Oklahoma 7 Aaron Gelvin, Contributor Promising, but Sooners struggle Oct 31, 2026; Norman, Oklahoma, USA; Oklahoma Sooners quarterback John Mateer (10) throws during the first quarter against the South Carolina Gamecocks at Gaylord Family-Oklahoma Memorial Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images As much as I'd like to believe that things are going to magically turn around, it's hard to create that expectation. Jason Witten may be the answer to what ails John Mateer and the Oklahoma Sooners offense. However, until we see it, there's no telling what you'll get from Witten's crew. Expect the defense to bounce back and play well against Jaden Baugh and the Gators' rushing attack, but with injury concerns in the secondary, the Sooners may have a hard time slowing down Tramell Jones.
